2f7f464.summary: Handles a click on a remnant (Aeldari/Necron body) card. Depending on card state it uses the Waystone, toggles the large card view, or restores a raised hand card; for enemy ambush cards it shows a face-down view. Mostly UI state; no network calls.
comments: Ignore the click if this body has no card attached
Need a BattleManager to know the UI state; a missing one is the compiler's null-check path
Choosing a resolution target: clicks on cards are blocked (only logged when dev tools are on)
Branch on the card's state: in hand, hand-showing, on board, or other
Aeldari remnant on board: a click spends the Waystone instead of opening the card view
Waystone usable: execute it and flag that we are waiting for it to resolve
Not a remnant: mark the card as being displayed and check whether the mulligan screen is visible
Card is raised in the player's hand (inHandShowing)
Hand click: opponent's cards can only be shown if they are Sabotage spells
Second click within 0.2s of the last one opens the large card display
Still raised in hand: put it back down, restore hand position, rotation and scale
Reset sorting layer, hide description and tooltips, and rewire the card's click listener (decompiler noise)
Other states: only a card in the middle of aiming an attack is handled, via the Waystone path above
Only open the large view in allowed UI states (or during the mulligan or tutorial rules)
Card was just clicked as a target: swallow this click so it does not also open the big view
A large card is already shown: leave it alone, otherwise build the card effects shown beside it
Show the card with its tier and the effects list in the large-card display
Enemy card in play with ambush: show it face-down with only the ambush icon, hiding stats and texts
Decompiler lost control flow here; this tail seems to enable the card-effect panel for non-environment cards
Enable the effect panel only if the effects apply, and not for environment cards

2f7f4e4.summary: Handles the pointer (mouse or touch) entering a remnant card. A hand card is raised and enlarged with description and tooltips; a board card gets its highlight changed, and if it is a valid target a combat damage preview and death icon are shown.
comments: Ignore if no card is attached
Ignore hovering while the right mouse button is held or with a multi-finger touch
UI state 0xe (choosing resolution target): hover is blocked, only logged with dev tools
Card state 2 is on board; anything else must be state 1 (in hand) and owned by the local player
Ask the BattleManager whether this hand card may be raised right now
Spread the other hand cards out and start raising this one
Work out the raised position; touch input uses a different Y offset from the mouse
Apply the new position, slightly toward the camera, and zero the rotation
Scale the card up to the device's hand-hover scale
Show description and tooltips, enlarge colliders, and show available targets
Decompiler garbage: the loop here is unrelated stack-pointer noise from inlined helpers; ignore it
Board card: skip hover effects in certain UI states (bitmask of busy states)
Highlight state 0 (regular) becomes selected; state 3 (potential target) goes to the target path below
Only remnant cards continue into the original-remnant card preview
Aeldari remnant: only show the preview on the owner's turn for the owner's cards
Hovering a valid target: mark it as the selected target and show the combat preview
Show the preview highlight on the attacker, unless in a state where it should not appear
Skip the damage preview while a Waystone use is resolving
Collect the damage values and types the attacker would deal to this card
Tactic cards deal their played damage (type 3) to the enemy target
Normal attack: if the target hits back, also add the damage it returns (type 4)
Ambush target: just hide the death icon, since damage is not shown for it
If the pending damage would kill the target, play the Minion Death icon
Finish: restore the original remnant view or clear the icon as needed

2f7f578.summary: Handles the pointer leaving a remnant card. Stops showing its description, puts a raised hand card back, clears combat preview highlights, and fades the highlight frame back to its normal state.
comments: Ignore if no card is attached
Stop showing the card's description
Own card that was raised in hand: lower it back
Clear this card's combat preview highlight
Also clear the preview on the card currently tracked as the attacker or target
Selected goes back to regular; selected-target-on-board goes back to potential target
Already in the target state: nothing to do
Switch the highlight state and show the frames
Per state: reset the frame colour and scale back (decompiler mixed up the variable names)
Potential target on board: recolour the frame and tween the scale back
Kill any running scale tween before starting a new one
Kill any running colour tween before starting a new one
Fade the frame colour back with a tween sequence, or set it straight away if no duration
Hide the overlay objects once the colour reset completes

2f7f6a4.summary: Switches a Necron remnant between its body form and remnant form. With animation it plays a random death animation and sound (to remnant) or the reanimate animation and sound; without animation it just toggles objects and the 3D body. Calls onComplete later.
comments: Store the callback; AnimationResurrectionEnd calls it when reanimation ends
Animated switch
option true: become a remnant (the body dies)
Hide the body model while the death animation plays
Pick a random death animation from the list
Decompiler glued DoDestroy-like code here: plays death sound, spawns death particles, destroys the object
Play the 3D death sound at this position if one is set
Spawn the death particle prefab and match its scale to this object
Use the chosen death animation on the VAT (vertex animation) player
option false: reanimate, so stop the idle remnant particles
Play the reanimate sound if one is set
Play the reanimate animation by name
Instant switch without animation: set the remnant object active or not
Show the 3D body only when not a remnant

2f7f824.summary: Called when a Necron remnant is destroyed. Plays the death sound at its position, spawns the death particle effect at the death particle position, and destroys the object.
comments: Play the death sound if one is set
Spawn the death particle effect at its configured position and rotation
If the effect has a script, hand it the card so it can show it
Match the effect's scale to this object, then destroy this object

2f7f828.summary: Returns the world position of this object's transform, used as the spawn point for death particles.

2f7f848.summary: Called when the reanimation animation finishes. Makes the Necron body visible again and invokes the completion callback saved by Toggle.
comments: Show the body again
Tell whoever started the toggle that the reanimation is done

2f7f9bc.summary: Runs every frame in a tutorial match. When the player clicks empty space (not UI, not ignored objects), flags the scripted AI manager to skip its current action. Does nothing in replays, non-tutorials, or when a window is open.
comments: Only run once the manager is fully initialised
Skipping is only allowed when the script says so
Never in replays
Only in tutorial matches
Ignore clicks while a window or popup is open
On mobile use the first touch, if it just began; otherwise use -1 for the mouse
Find out whether the pointer is over UI; UI clicks do not count
Only react on the frame the mouse button goes down
Cast a ray from the camera through the click and see if it hits any non-ignored object
Nothing hit: empty space click, so skip the AI's next scripted action

2f7f9d0.summary: Same check as the tutorial manager's per-frame Update: on a click in empty space during a tutorial match, flags the scripted AI to skip its next action.
comments: Skipping is only allowed when the script says so
Never in replays
Only in tutorial matches
Ignore clicks while a window or popup is open
On mobile use the first touch, if it just began; otherwise -1 for the mouse
UI clicks do not count
Only react on the frame the mouse button goes down
Cast a ray from the click point against everything except ignored layers
Nothing hit: empty space, so skip the AI's next scripted action

2f7fce4.summary: Builds the name of a scripted turn, such as 'Player 2' or 'AI 2', from who starts the match and the turn number, and stores it in turnName.
comments: Parity of the turn number (0 or 1)
Round number is turn/2 plus one; the INFINITY test is the float-to-int overflow guard
Default is the AI; the Player prefix is used when the parity matches the starting side
Join the prefix and round number and store it

2f7fe2c.summary: Loads the localized tutorial text for this scripted action and expands its placeholders: modular descriptions, card names, melee/ranged/reanimate keywords, trait names and Energy sprites. Returns the finished string.
comments: Look up the text under TutorialData/ using the reference key (with the PC suffix for PC tips)
Empty text: return as is
Text has modular description markers: expand each one
Find every marker with a regex and loop over the matches (compiler-generated enumerator and dispose code)
Marker holds comma-separated parts: the term name, then optional values
Look up the Modular_Description term and fill in its arguments from parts 1 and 2
Replace the marker in the text with the expanded description
Decompiler dumped the enumerator cleanup (Dispose in finally blocks) here; it is not game logic
Next: card name markers, found by a second regex
Next: keyword markers (melee, ranged, reanimate)
Last: Energy markers, for numbers 0 to 8
Replace each Energy number marker with the matching Energy sprite tag
Keywords: replace each marker with the bold localized word from MainMenu/General
Traits: loop over every DefinedTrait value and replace its marker with the trait's display name
Card markers: loop over matches (decompiler placed this at the end)
Use the localized Card_Name term as a fallback
If the player data is available, find the card in the full card collection and use its localized name

2f7ff20.summary: Returns this action's text reference key, with '-PC' appended when it is a PC-specific tip.
comments: PC tips use a separate text key with the -PC suffix
Empty key: result is just the suffix (or empty)
Concatenate key and suffix (inlined string concat)

2f7ff80.summary: Rebuilds the editor display name (actionType) for a scripted action from its first data entry. Chat, tip and radio actions get their localized text appended; actions by a unit get a unit label; some actions get a target name.
comments: No data: name it Undefined
Start with the name of the action type enum
Text-based types (AI/player chat, big chat, small tip, radio): append the localized text
For certain action types (hex ids; they seem to be unit-acting actions) add who acts
Warlord actors get an Enemy warlord or Player warlord label
Otherwise append the first target's name if there is one
Type 0x8c also appends a target name

2f804fc.summary: Returns true if any entry in this scripted action's data list is of the activate-hand-cards type (0xaa).
comments: Loop through the data entries
Found one of type 0xaa (activate hand cards): stop, i is below _size so the result is true

2f805a4.summary: Checks whether a battle action, with its acting card and target card, matches what this scripted tutorial step expects. Used to decide if the player's move advances the script. Returns true when type, actor and target all fit.
comments: First check the action type: does the real battle action fit the expected scripted type?
PlayCard: must be a card played from hand
If a minion-position rule applies, work out whether the card would land left of the target
Wanted 'left' but it lands elsewhere, or wanted 'not left' but it lands left: no match
Attack: a normal attack or its continuation
Free-mode attack: only a few action types are allowed (bitmask)
Change-to-ranged/melee types: seem to be matched by an attack or an attack change
Active ability, end turn, tap card (Waystone use matches at once)
Now check the actor: Warlord must be a Hero; minion types must be non-Hero and the same unique card
Unexpected actor type: log an error
No target card: matches already
Target Warlord: must be a Hero on the player's or enemy's side as expected
Target minion or hand card: must not be a Hero, and must be the exact card if one is named
Check the side: a player minion must be on the player's side, an enemy minion on the other
